q: MTF (Margin Trading Facility) requires the client to put in at least what minimum margin?
e: MTF: minimum 50% initial margin (cash + approved securities). Daily MTM. Securities held in a separate 'MTF demat' account. Only Group I securities are eligible.
Only Group I (highest-liquidity) stocks are MTF-eligible. T-Group, Z-Group penny stocks are excluded for client safety. Daily MTM applied.
NRE PIS = fully repatriable. NRO PIS = non-repatriable / limited (India-sourced funds only). The two routes have different tax + remittance implications.

q: ASBA via UPI for retail IPO has a cap of:
e: UPI mechanism for ASBA retail IPO is capped at ₹5 lakh per application. Above this, retail must use net banking ASBA.

q: Currency derivatives in India are traded primarily in:
e: Currency derivatives in India: INR pairs (USD/INR, EUR/INR, GBP/INR, JPY/INR) on NSE/BSE/MSEI. Tick size 0.25 paise. Hedging documentation required for amounts > USD 100 million per FY.

q: Commodity derivatives in India are regulated by:
e: Commodity derivatives are regulated by SEBI since the FMC merger in 2015. Earlier under FMC (Forward Markets Commission). Regulated under SEBI Act + Securities Contracts Act.

q: A research analyst at a brokerage that also runs investment-banking activities must maintain:
o: Chinese walls between research and IB / proprietary trading
e: Chinese walls = procedural and informational barriers preventing exchange of price-sensitive information between research, investment banking, and proprietary trading desks. Mandatory under SEBI conduct norms.

q: Brokers under SEBI's CSCRF must report cyber-security breaches within:
e: CSCRF (Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Framework) mandates breach reporting within 6 hours of detection. Annual audits + cyber drills also mandatory.

q: SEBI's IA (Investment Adviser) Regulations were issued in:
e: SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations 2013 govern fee-only investment advisers. SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations 2014 govern research analysts. Separate registration regimes.

q: An investor's Capital Gains Statement (CGS) from the broker is used for:
e: CGS provides realized capital gains by year (STCG / LTCG split) for income-tax filing. Brokers also issue STT certificates and holding statements.

q: DPDPA (Digital Personal Data Protection Act) was enacted in:
e: DPDPA 2023 establishes data privacy obligations for fiduciaries handling personal data. Brokers (handling investor PII) are 'data fiduciaries' under DPDPA — subject to consent + purpose-limitation rules.

q: Anchor investors in an IPO get an allocation of QIB portion up to approximately:
e: Anchor allocation can be up to 60% of the QIB portion. Anchor investors commit before public issue, with 30-day lock-in (longer lock-ins on portions per recent SEBI updates).
